title: Exact exponential separation between auxiliary-variable projections and retained-variable CNFs
claim: For any k >= 1 and block sizes m_1, ..., m_k >= 0 with M = sum(m_r) retained variables x_{r,i} and k auxiliary selectors z_1, ..., z_k, the (1 + M)-clause coupled selector CNF Phi = (z_1 | ... | z_k) & AND_{r,i} (~z_r | x_{r,i}) projects existentially onto F(x) = OR_{r=1}^k AND_{i=1}^{m_r} x_{r,i}. Every list-CNF over {x_{r,i}} alone pointwise equivalent to F—allowing arbitrary literal signs, widths, repeated literals, duplicates, and tautologies—requires at least prod(m_r) clauses, achieved tightly by the canonical distribution. Splitting the coupling clause with k - 2 Tseitin variables gives an exact 3-CNF projection with (k - 1) + M clauses (k >= 2, width <= 3), yielding an exponential separation (3k - 2 3-clauses vs. 2^k width-k clauses when m_r = 2). This is a nonformal note with reproducible Python checks, not a Lean proof or P-versus-NP separation.
novelty: Accepted contribution PR #46 proved a tight mn clause lower bound for eliminating one selector over retained variables and flagged auxiliary variables as an open change of model. This note gives the tight multi-selector counterpart: coupling k selectors in one disjunction turns the cost of eliminating auxiliary variables from additive to multiplicative (prod m_r), proves the fooling-set lower bound for arbitrary signed list-CNFs, quantifies the linear 3-CNF compression, and compares against PR #22 falsifying-row counts and PR #14 resolution refutations.

prior_art.relationship: Direct motivation: proves the tight mn bound for single-selector elimination over retained variables and notes that allowing auxiliary variables changes the question. This note generalizes the fooling-set bound to k coupled selectors and quantifies the auxiliary-variable compression.

Provides the truth-table certificate counting methodology and comparison against PR #19/PR #14; this note computes the falsifying-row count prod(2^{m_r} - 1) (3^k for m_r = 2) on the coupled selector family.
Defines the repository's list-resolution checker, contrasted here via a 2k-step refutation of Phi under unit-falsifying assumptions.

limitations: This is a nonformal research note, not a Lean-checked theorem. The prod(m_r) clause lower bound applies to pointwise Boolean equivalence over the retained variables without auxiliary variables; allowing auxiliary variables yields linear size. Finite Python verification covers k = 1..4 (m_r = 2) and exhaustive general-CNF minimality up to M = 4; general parameters rely on the written mathematical proof. No general resolution lower bound, Extended Resolution lower bound, or P-versus-NP claim is made.
